  Line or code reference: line 480 (`refspecs = positionals[1:] if len(positionals) > 1 or not remote_provided else positionals`) and the identical line in workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:480
  Problem: With `--repo=<repo>` and a single positional that names a remote (e.g. `git push --repo=upstream origin`), the new logic falls into the `else positionals` branch and treats `origin` as a refspec instead of as the destination remote.
  Why it fails at runtime: Git's documented push syntax is `git push [<options>] [<repository> [<refspec>...]]`; `--repo=` overrides repository discovery but does NOT replace the positional remote. After the autofix the guard will try to look up a branch named `origin`, fail to resolve it, and emit the "could not resolve git push refspec" warning — surfacing a spurious confirmation request for a syntactically valid command. The pre-autofix live-copy logic (`refspecs = positionals[1:] if positionals else []`) handled this case correctly; the autofix regressed it while syncing to the template's previously-broken behaviour.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

  Line or code reference: 480-486, `refspecs = positionals[1:] if len(positionals) > 1 or not remote_provided else positionals`
  Problem: When `--repo` is present with exactly one positional argument, the parser treats that argument as a refspec. The adjacent comment and tests establish that a positional repository takes precedence over `--repo`; in this case the argument is the repository and there are no explicit refspecs.
  Why it fails at runtime: For a command such as `git push --repo=upstream origin`, the guard checks a branch named `origin` instead of the current branch and its configured default push destination. It therefore does not inspect the branch and commit the push will actually target.

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: line 480 (refspecs = positionals[1:] if len(positionals) > 1 or not remote_provided else positionals)
  Problem: When --repo is provided and exactly one positional argument is given (e.g., git push --repo=upstream origin), the guard treats that positional as a refspec instead of recognizing it as the remote repository.
  Why it fails at runtime: The guard will attempt to look up a branch named "origin" via query_pull_requests, producing either a misleading merged-PR check against the wrong branch or an unnecessary confirmation request. Git's actual behavior is to treat the first positional as the remote regardless of whether --repo is present; only when there are zero or multiple positionals does --repo become the effective remote. The current logic only handles the multi-positional case correctly (len > 1 branch) but fails on the single-positional case (else branch returns positionals unchanged).
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
